rules.title: CCCL Patron Conduct Policy (2026)
rules.summary: Requires patrons to be engaged in activities associated with public-library use and regulates disruption, obstruction, harassment, noise, and staff-directed compliance. It does not expressly resolve peaceful recording. Whether recording/information gathering may be excluded under the library-purpose clause remains activity-specific.
rules.constitutional_test: LPF purpose/reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality; separate recording doctrine where recording is restricted
rules.enforcement_hook: Policy allows removal/suspension; criminal enforcement requires separate statutory authority.
open_questions: Does CCCL interpret peaceful recording/information gathering as library-purpose activity?
What staff training governs camera encounters?

rules.title: CCCL Suspension Policy (2026)
applies_to: all CCCL facilities covered by suspension
rules.summary: Creates escalating suspension periods and states that return during suspension may lead to law-enforcement contact and arrest for trespass under Penal Code §602. The policy does not itself identify the exact criminal subsection/elements.
rules.constitutional_test: Due process + underlying validity of the conduct rule + element-specific trespass analysis
rules.enforcement_hook: Generic reference to Penal Code §602; exact subsection and predicates unresolved.
open_questions: What internal criteria govern one-day versus longer suspensions?
What notice/appeal records exist?
What exact §602 subsection is used in practice?

rules.title: Children and Teen Area Policy
rules.summary: Reserves designated children/teen areas primarily to intended age groups and accompanying or collection-using patrons at staff discretion. The policy does not itself create a systemwide camera ban.
rules.constitutional_test: Area-purpose reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality; recording restrictions require separate analysis
rules.enforcement_hook: Staff may redirect access; downstream removal authority depends on applicable policy/statute.
open_questions: How is staff discretion constrained and trained?
Are any branch-specific camera rules layered onto these areas?

rules.title: CCCL Meeting Room Rules
rules.summary: Opens meeting rooms for defined educational/cultural/community uses under reservation rules. Individual subject/use restrictions must be tested within the limited public forum rather than assumed valid from the existence of the room rules.
rules.enforcement_hook: Reservation/use terms; removal requires independent access/enforcement authority where disputed.
open_questions: What Concord-specific room terms are currently imposed in practice?
Are recording rules imposed on room users?

rules.title: Rules for Exhibits / Display / Distribution of Non-Library Materials
rules.summary: The County intentionally opens exhibit/display/distribution channels for cultural, educational, or civic material while expressly excluding religious services/activities and advocacy or support for a political party or candidate, and requiring authorization. Those subject/content restrictions require a channel-specific limited-public-forum analysis; the policy text itself supplies enough information to begin that constitutional test without CPRA.
open_questions: Whether each subject restriction is reasonable in light of the specific opened channel and viewpoint neutral under current Ninth Circuit doctrine.
How the restrictions are applied at Concord in practice.
Whether any branch-specific additional rules have been adopted.

rules.title: Self-Service Sundays Access Agreement / Program Conditions
rules.summary: The current June 2026 agreement is public. It requires compliance with all library policies and with announcements/directions from library staff, security, County agents, or the PA system; refusal to leave if asked may lead to suspension. It also states that some interior/exterior areas may be monitored by security cameras and encourages patrons to carry a phone. The direction/refusal clauses cannot be treated as self-validating authority for an otherwise unconstitutional command.
rules.constitutional_test: Conditioned-access/LPF analysis + unconstitutional-conditions concerns where expressive rights are burdened
rules.enforcement_hook: Conditioned-access agreement and library suspension process; any criminal enforcement still requires independent legal authority.
open_questions: What internal guidance limits or interprets directions given by security/County agents during Self-Service Sundays?
What rule, if any, governs patron photography/recording during the program?

rules.title: California Government Code §7927.105 — Library Patron Records
rules.summary: Protects qualifying library-maintained patron records from disclosure. It is a confidentiality duty governing records, not by its text a categorical camera prohibition on ordinary patrons.
rules.constitutional_test: Use as privacy-context authority; any visitor recording restriction still requires independent legal basis.
rules.enforcement_hook: Public-records confidentiality rule, not a general patron camera offense.

rules.title: California Penal Code §632 — Confidential Communications
rules.summary: Can directly regulate intentional recording of a confidential communication; applicability depends on objective circumstances and statutory exclusions. It is not a blanket indoor-audio prohibition.
rules.constitutional_test: Statutory elements + First Amendment analysis where protected recording is burdened
rules.enforcement_hook: Penal Code §632 where elements are met.
open_questions: Which library interactions, if any, objectively qualify as confidential communications?

rules.title: California Trespass / Public-Agency Obstruction Statutes
rules.summary: California trespass and public-agency-obstruction doctrine is now researched at the statewide level. Facility application remains element- and fact-specific; a policy violation or leave demand does not by itself establish the applicable statutory predicates.
rules.constitutional_test: Exact statutory elements + constitutional savings clause + validity of underlying exclusion
rules.enforcement_hook: Penal Code §§602/602.1 only when the selected subsection/elements are satisfied.
open_questions: Which subsection does CCCL actually request police to use after suspension/refusal?

rules.title: CCCL Patron Conduct Policy — Panhandling / Soliciting Donations
applies_to: library property, including potentially exterior areas covered by the policy
rules.summary: The current policy prohibits panhandling and soliciting donations or contributions on library property, and the Suspension Policy places this conduct in the one-day-to-one-week category. That breadth creates an immediate area-specific constitutional question because Concord's Registry includes exterior subareas classified TPF/HIGH, while the ordinary interior is purpose-limited. The same words may therefore face materially different scrutiny depending on where they are enforced.
rules.constitutional_test: TPF: applicable speech/solicitation time-place-manner scrutiny; LPF interior: purpose/reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality
rules.enforcement_hook: Library removal/suspension policy; any arrest requires separate statutory authority.
open_questions: Whether CCCL applies this prohibition to peaceful charitable solicitation on exterior TPF-classified areas.
Whether the County distinguishes passive requests/signs from direct solicitation.
What factual justification supports the property-wide scope.

rules.title: Concord Municipal Code ch. 9.08 — Solicitation Location Restrictions
rules.summary: Concord prohibits solicitation in any public parking lot or structure and within 30 feet of a queue of five or more persons, among other locations. This is directly material to the Library's public lots and potentially entrance queues. The California Supreme Court upheld a different Los Angeles solicitation scheme whose parking-lot restriction applied after dark; Concord's all-times parking-lot text is broader and requires its own analysis rather than borrowing that result.
rules.constitutional_test: California Speech Clause + First Amendment forum/time-place-manner analysis, mapped to each exact Library subarea
rules.enforcement_hook: Infraction; three or more violations within one year may be charged as a misdemeanor under the ordinance.
open_questions: How §9.08.040 is applied to peaceful solicitation in the Library's TPF-classified exterior areas.
Whether passive signs or responses to inquiries fall outside the ordinance's definition of solicitation.

cpra_targets.target: Current CCCL internal staff/security guidance, training, scripts, supervisor instructions, and sign templates addressing photography, video/audio recording, observation, information gathering, solicitation, or the 'library-purpose activity' clause, including Concord-specific material.
cpra_targets.why: The public rules expose constitutional questions but do not show how staff are trained to apply them. This single system-level request can replace several narrower duplicate requests.

cpra_targets.target: Current implementation guidance for suspensions/removals, including the Penal Code subsection(s) or law-enforcement instructions relied on when a suspended patron refuses to leave, and any instructions for one-day through one-week suspensions.
cpra_targets.why: The public policy cites Penal Code §602 generically and provides an express appeal only for suspensions longer than one week; implementation records could clarify the enforcement and process actually used.

cpra_targets.target: Records from the last three years identifying incidents or complaints in which recording, photography, peaceful solicitation, or non-disruptive information gathering was cited as a basis for removal or suspension at Concord Library, including the policy cited and disposition.
cpra_targets.why: Would test actual interpretation, selective enforcement, and whether the newly identified solicitation/recording issues are merely theoretical.
